rows.sos_note: Faced MIA (12th), CHI (24th), NYJ (4th), LV (25th), BUF (13th) (defense vs WRs rank). Those defenses allowed 8% more yards per target to WRs than average, so recent games adjust to 22.1 (raw 24.5).
rows.why: Check the news first — news: promoted: Beat preview: Patriots to lean on Chism, Kyle Williams and DeMario Douglas without A.J. Brown. (Boston Globe live blog). Mixed signals: the matchup points to the under, recent games don't. We expect about 25.8 receiving yards vs the 30.5 line (needs 53% to pay at -115)
rows.why_long: Hard Rock under 30.5 at -115 needs 53% to pay; fair after the vig 51%. Averaging 24.5 over the last 8 games, lower than 30.5 in 49% of them (raw 63%, shrunk 53%). GB allows -5% to WRs → projects 25.8 (raw 64%, shrunk 54%).
why_points: The bet: Rec yds under 30.5 at -115. To make money it has to win 53% of the time. The betting market, with the sportsbook's cut removed, gives it 51%.
Game log, most recent first: 37, 16, 0, 57, 42, 1, -2, 35. Weighted average 24.5; went lower than 30.5 in 4 of 8 games (49% recency-weighted).
Trending down: last 3 games average 17.7 vs 26.6 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±20.3, so the line is 0.3 of those swings above his average (standard deviations) — a modest gap.
Market: ESPN Bet make this side 51% once their cut is removed; Hard Rock's price needs 53%. Hard Rock charges more than the market for this side.
Matchup: GB has allowed -5% vs the league average to WRs (already shrunk toward average for sample size).
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): -9% on his average.
PFF: GB plays man on 18% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 27%); he gains 1.94 yds/route vs man and 1.43 vs zone → -3% from scheme.
PFF: GB allows 1.43 yds/route to WRs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.56) → -9% against his usual opponents.

PFF: He runs 33% of his routes from the slot (1.68 yds/route there, 1.43 outside); GB allows 1.20 yds/route to slot WRs and 1.65 outside (league 1.48 / 1.61, opponent-adjusted) → -6% vs his usual opponents.
Projection: we expect 25.8 receiving yards on average; in a typical game 18.8 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 11.7 below the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 63% and the matchup 64%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 53%, matchup 54%.
Bottom line: we give it 54% to win and it needs 53%. The edge is the difference: +0.1 points; that works out to about +0¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
rows.glance_head: Mixed: the matchup favors the under, his recent games don't (we expect about 18.8 in a typical game vs the 30.5 line).
